## In-Class Agenda

- What do we mean when we “clean” or create culture as data?
- Manually Data Cleaning
- Data Biographies
- Accuracy vs Power
- Data archeologies and metadata
- databases
- Debate: how should we decide what data to extract and how do our choices determine how we understand the data?

## Assigned Materials

- Rawson, Katie, and Trevor Muñoz. “Against Cleaning.” In *Debates in the Digital Humanities 2019*, edited by Matthew K. Gold and Lauren F. Klein, 279–92. University of Minnesota Press, 2019. [https://doi.org/10.5749/j.ctvg251hk.26](https://doi.org/10.5749/j.ctvg251hk.26).
- Lurie, Stephen. “A History of Menus Is a Menu of History.” *The Pudding*, June 2026. [https://pudding.cool/2026/06/menu-story](https://pudding.cool/2026/06/menu-story).
- Daniels, Matt. “5,000 Restaurant Menus, Years 1880-1920.” *The Pudding*, June 2026. [https://pudding.cool/2026/06/menu-collection](https://pudding.cool/2026/06/menu-collection).
- Cegłowski, Maciej. “Deep-Fried Data.” *Idle Words*, September 27, 2016. [https://idlewords.com/talks/deep_fried_data.htm](https://idlewords.com/talks/deep_fried_data.htm).
